questions.q: Per this lesson, which role is usually responsible for deciding what values belong in a picklist and for reviewing duplicate-record reports for business accuracy?
options: The business data steward
The data custodian
The governance committee only
The external auditor
questions.explain: The business data steward is the functional, day-to-day role that owns quality decisions like picklist values and reviewing duplicate reports -- they're closest to the actual data.

questions.q: In most Salesforce orgs, which stewardship role does the Salesforce admin typically fill?
options: The data owner, with full authority to decide what gets enforced
The external compliance auditor
The technical/platform steward, who implements decisions in configuration but doesn't unilaterally set what gets enforced
No role at all -- admins are excluded from the stewardship model
questions.explain: The admin is usually the technical/platform steward: they have authority over how something is implemented (Validation Rules, Matching Rules, Flow) but not over what the business decides should be enforced.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the data custodian's responsibility?
options: Deciding which picklist values are meaningful to the business
Approving a company's annual marketing budget
Writing the Lead Source field's help text
Infrastructure-level controls such as Shield Platform Encryption key management, backup/recovery, and data residency
questions.explain: The data custodian handles the infrastructure/security layer -- encryption keys, backups, data residency, integration security -- which is a different scope than the business or technical steward roles.

questions.q: What two problems does this lesson say result from one person (typically the admin) being implicitly expected to act as owner, business steward, technical steward, AND custodian all at once?
options: They become a single point of failure for every data decision, and nobody outside IT feels accountable for data quality since the role structure never asked them to be
Nothing goes wrong; consolidating all roles in one person is the most efficient structure
Salesforce technically blocks one user from holding multiple permission sets
The org automatically loses its Salesforce support contract
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names these two failure modes: the admin becomes a bottleneck for decisions they may not be positioned to make, and the business never develops its own sense of accountability for data quality.

questions.q: In the phone-number-formatting handoff example, who should decide whether Matching Rules should now also compare on email as a fallback, and why?
options: The business data steward alone, since it's a day-to-day configuration tweak
The data custodian, since email addresses are considered infrastructure data
The data owner, because it's a standards-level decision about how duplicates should be defined, not just an implementation fix
No one -- Matching Rule logic can never be changed once configured
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes a pure implementation fix (technical steward's job) from a standards decision like changing what fields count toward a duplicate match, which requires the data owner's involvement.
